terms.comment: Classically a questioning, an inquiry, the examination of witnesses (Lewis & Short); Traupman gives it for an opinion poll. Rome counted votes, not opinions: for voting, see vote and election.

evidence: M-O s.v. poll (public opinion), after Egger
terms.comment: A coinage from Greek δῆμος and σκοπεῖν, with the adjective dēmoscopicus (Egger).

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 354, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. poll (public opinion).
